evidence_chain: Fact: FormFactor's investor relations site lists the company as Nasdaq: FORM and shows an active 2026 IR calendar, including investor day and earnings-related materials. Source: https://investors.formfactor.com/ ; https://investors.formfactor.com/investor-relations

Fact: FormFactor's Q1 2026 press release said it delivered record DRAM revenue with increased demand in HBM applications and sustained demand in non-HBM applications, and that Foundry & Logic demand rose on probe cards for networking applications. Source: https://investors.formfactor.com/news-releases/news-release-details/formfactor-inc-reports-2026-first-quarter-results

Fact: FormFactor's June 2, 2026 blog post states that AI, HBM, advanced packaging, chiplets, and silicon photonics are creating new testing challenges, and says HBM has become essential for AI accelerators and HPC systems. Source: https://www.formfactor.com/blog/2026/how-ai-and-hbm-are-redefining-semiconductor-test/

Fact: FormFactor's blog and investor materials emphasize probe cards, wafer probing, and advanced test subsystems as core offerings. Source: https://www.formfactor.com/ ; https://www.formfactor.com/blog/

Fact: FormFactor's May 13, 2026 investor/news material claims top customer-satisfaction ranking in test subsystems and explicitly references HBM and advanced packaging as end-market relevance. Source: https://investors.formfactor.com/news-releases/news-release-details/formfactor-sets-global-standard-1-test-subsystems-and-focused

Fact: The investor day deck snippet contains 'Next Gen HBM 4E / 5', which is a direct signal that management is framing a next-generation HBM cycle. Source: https://investors.formfactor.com/static-files/29f1154b-e1e4-4b57-afbd-f296b3f36504
Inference: If management continues to separate HBM/DRAM growth from the broader memory cycle and shows margin support from advanced probe cards, the AI thesis strengthens materially.
Inference: If HBM4E/5 qualification expands across multiple DRAM customers, FormFactor's role may be closer to an AI memory chokepoint than the market currently prices.
falsification_plan: Check whether future 10-Q/10-K and earnings calls continue to separate HBM-specific growth from general memory recovery.
Look for gross margin bridge and product-mix evidence showing advanced probe cards are accretive.
Verify whether multiple DRAM customers, not just one, are contributing to HBM probe-card demand.
Track whether HBM4/HBM4E mentions move from roadmap language to revenue, bookings, or backlog language.
If management stops emphasizing HBM or frames growth mainly as conventional DRAM/NAND cyclical recovery, downgrade the thesis.
deep_reports.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether HBM probe-card shipments are expanding across all three major DRAM makers, whether DRAM/HBM mix is lifting gross margin, and whether HBM4/HBM4E qualification creates a durable upgrade cycle rather than a one-time demand spike.
next_research_tasks: Pull the latest 10-K, 10-Q, and full earnings-call transcript and isolate all HBM, DRAM, probe-card, backlog, and customer-concentration mentions.
Compare Q/Q revenue and gross-margin bridges to see whether mix improvement is tied to advanced probe cards.
Map named or implied memory customers and test whether there is evidence across Samsung, SK hynix, and Micron-related demand.
Review the investor day deck for any quantitative HBM4E/5 roadmap, capacity, or qualification commentary.
Check competitor commentary and industry trade coverage for probe-card share shifts and qualification wins.
risks: HBM may be a small contributor relative to conventional DRAM/NAND recovery, limiting the AI-specific upside.
Customer concentration could be high if only one major memory maker is driving demand.
Competitors could win probe-card share or force pricing pressure.
Gross margin may fail to improve if advanced-memory mix does not scale.
HBM4/HBM4E timing could slip, or qualification may not convert into sustained revenue.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: Wafer-level semiconductor test; advanced probe cards; test subsystems; memory/DRAM validation layer between wafer fabrication and packaging, especially relevant for HBM qualification and yield learning.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: FormFactor 的核心价值不只是周期性半导体测试设备，而是 AI 驱动下 HBM/DDR5/先进封装带来的晶圆级测试复杂度上升。随着 HBM 需要更严格的 Known Good Die 验证、更多堆叠层数和更高良率要求，高端探针卡和相关测试子系统可能成为量产与爬坡中的必要环节。2026 年公司披露已明确提到 DRAM 收入创纪录、HBM 需求提升，以及 HBM4E / 5 相关信息，说明 AI 内存测试链条正在进入更高代际。需要继续验证的是：这是否真的是可持续的 HBM 特定升级周期，而不是广义存储复苏。
deep_reports.thesis_en: [Hypothesis] FormFactor’s value is not just a cyclical semiconductor test-equipment story; it may be an AI-driven wafer-level test bottleneck created by HBM, DDR5, and advanced packaging complexity. As HBM requires stricter Known Good Die validation, more stacked dies, and tighter yield requirements, high-end probe cards and related test subsystems can become a necessary part of volume ramp and yield learning. Company disclosures in 2026 explicitly referenced record DRAM revenue, increased HBM demand, and HBM4E / 5-related materials, suggesting the AI-memory test chain is moving into a new generation. The key open question is whether this is a durable HBM-specific upgrade cycle or mostly a broad memory recovery story.
deep_reports.title_cn: HBM 量产的隐藏卡点：FormFactor 的高端探针卡能否持续绑定 AI 内存复杂度
deep_reports.title_en: Hidden chokepoint in HBM ramp: can FormFactor’s advanced probe cards stay tied to AI memory complexity?
deep_reports.why_underfollowed: The market may still bucket FORM as a cyclical semiconductor test/probe-card vendor rather than as an AI memory-bandwidth enabler. The AI link is hidden in test complexity, customer qualification, and product mix, not in obvious GPU or accelerator revenue. That makes it easier to miss in broad AI screens.

evidence_chain: Fact: PTI's official website describes the company as a leading provider of turnkey services for chip probing, packaging, and testing. Source: https://www.pti.com.tw/

Fact: PTI's TWSE company profile states that Powertech Technology Inc. was founded in 1997 and provides turnkey service for chip probe, packaging, testing, and product delivery for various memory and logic devices. Source: https://www.twse.com.tw/pdf/en/6239_en.pdf

Fact: PTI's official About page says the company serves international customers with chip bumping, chip probing, IC assembly, final testing, burn-in, and system-level assembly. Source: https://www.pti.com.tw/en/about/about

Fact: PTI's official product/service pages list wafer-level packaging, chip probing for memory and logic devices, flip-chip/FCBGA, final test for DRAM, NOR Flash, NAND Flash, MCP and logic devices, wire-bond BGA, and module assembly. Source: https://www.pti.com.tw/

Fact: PTI's official financial page shows consolidated revenue by service for 2025 of NT$50,200m packaging, NT$16,662m testing, NT$8,067m SiP/Module, and NT$74,929m total revenue. Source: https://www.pti.com.tw/en/ir/financial
Fact: PTI's official financial page shows packaging represented 67% of 2025 consolidated revenue, testing 22%, and SiP/Module 11%. Source: https://www.pti.com.tw/en/ir/financial

Inference: Because PTI has a large packaging/testing revenue base and provides services for memory devices, it is a plausible beneficiary if memory IDMs outsource more conventional memory backend work during HBM prioritization.
Hypothesis: AI/HBM demand is already creating measurable overflow demand for PTI. This is not yet directly proven by the supplied evidence.

Speculation requiring verification: FOPLP, PiFO, CPO, or advanced-packaging/test revenue could create an additional AI-related chokepoint for PTI if disclosed as material; the supplied evidence does not yet confirm material revenue from these items.
falsification_plan: Falsify if PTI's latest annual reports, quarterly reports, or investor-conference materials contain no meaningful discussion of AI, HBM, HPC, advanced packaging, high-end test, FOPLP, PiFO, CPO, capacity tightness, or customer outsourcing.
Falsify if monthly revenue improves while gross margin, operating margin, utilization, or pricing commentary remains weak, suggesting ordinary cycle rebound rather than bottleneck economics.
Falsify if capex is maintenance-oriented or legacy-memory-oriented with no evidence of advanced memory backend, test, wafer-level packaging, or high-performance packaging expansion.
Falsify if memory customers publicly indicate they are keeping conventional DRAM/NAND backend work in-house rather than outsourcing because of HBM prioritization.
Falsify if PTI's SiP/Module, testing, or advanced-packaging-related businesses remain flat or immaterial despite broader AI/HBM growth.

Falsify if management attributes growth mainly to broad consumer electronics, commodity memory restocking, or inventory normalization, with no signs of structural outsourcing or capacity allocation pressure.
deep_reports.hidden_signal_to_verify: The hidden signal is whether HBM prioritization by memory IDMs is causing conventional DRAM/NAND packaging, testing, burn-in, or module overflow into PTI, and whether that is visible in company-level numbers. Upgrade evidence would include: explicit management commentary on HBM/AI/HPC-driven outsourcing; rising utilization and gross margin not explainable only by commodity memory recovery; capex aimed at advanced memory backend, wafer-level packaging, FOPLP, PiFO, CPO, or high-end test; customer disclosures indicating outsourced conventional-memory backend due to internal HBM focus; and product/segment revenue showing advanced packaging/test is becoming material.
next_research_tasks: Download and review PTI's latest annual report and the last 4 quarterly reports. Extract mentions of AI, HBM, HPC, advanced packaging, high-end test, wafer-level packaging, FOPLP, PiFO, CPO, utilization, pricing, customer allocation, and capex.

Review PTI's institutional investor conference materials and webcast transcripts, if available, for management commentary on memory demand, customer outsourcing, advanced packaging, testing demand, and margin drivers.

Build a monthly revenue and gross-margin tracker from 2023 to the latest available month. Look for divergence between revenue growth and margin expansion that could indicate capacity tightness rather than only cyclical recovery.
Compare PTI's packaging/testing/SiP revenue mix over 2020-2025. Test whether testing or SiP/Module is gaining share in a way consistent with higher-value AI/HPC backend demand.
Search customer-side disclosures from major memory IDMs for comments on HBM capacity allocation, conventional DRAM/NAND backend outsourcing, and OSAT partner capacity.

Check Taiwan exchange announcements and Market Observation Post System filings for capex, plant expansion, equipment purchases, related-party/customer concentration changes, or advanced-packaging project disclosures.

Map PTI against reference OSAT and test peers: FormFactor as a more direct HBM test reference, ASE/SPIL/Amkor as OSAT scale references, and memory-IDM captive backend capacity as the substitution risk.

Verify whether PTI has official disclosures or patents related to FOPLP, PiFO, CPO, high-bandwidth memory test, advanced memory packaging, or system-level test. Upgrade only if revenue or capex materiality is visible.

Interview or collect third-party industry commentary from packaging/test equipment suppliers on whether conventional memory backend outsourcing is increasing because HBM consumes internal memory-IDM resources.

Create an upgrade/downgrade scorecard: upgrade if there is explicit AI/HBM/customer-overflow evidence plus margin/utilization improvement; downgrade if the data only shows commodity memory-cycle recovery.
risks: Evidence gap risk: current supplied evidence confirms PTI's OSAT position but does not directly link PTI revenue, utilization, capex, or margins to AI, HBM, HPC, CPO, FOPLP, or PiFO.
Cycle confusion risk: revenue improvement could be a normal DRAM/NAND cycle recovery rather than a structural AI/HBM overflow signal.
Pricing-power risk: if PTI gains volume but not pricing or margin, the thesis may be lower quality and less chokepoint-like.
Customer-allocation risk: memory IDMs may retain more backend work internally or allocate outsourcing to other OSATs, reducing PTI-specific benefit.

Technology-positioning risk: PTI may remain concentrated in mature memory backend services while the highest AI/HBM value capture accrues to substrate, bonding, TSV, advanced test, or leading-edge packaging players.
Disclosure risk: even if overflow exists, PTI may not disclose enough customer or product detail to prove the thesis with high confidence.
Competitive risk: larger OSATs or memory-IDM captive capacity may absorb the overflow before PTI sees durable utilization or pricing benefits.
Capex execution risk: if PTI invests ahead of confirmed demand, margins and free cash flow could be pressured.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: AI demand driver -> GPU/AI server growth -> HBM demand growth -> memory IDM internal allocation toward HBM and advanced memory -> potential crowding out of conventional DRAM/NAND backend work -> third-party OSAT assembly/test/burn-in/module overflow -> PTI as memory-heavy OSAT. Supported facts: PTI provides turnkey services for chip probing, packaging, testing, and product delivery for memory and logic devices; PTI offers wafer-level packaging, chip probing for memory and logic, flip-chip/FCBGA, final test for DRAM/NOR/NAND/MCP/logic, wire-bond BGA, and module assembly. Inference: these capabilities make PTI a plausible recipient of memory back-end overflow if HBM prioritization tightens IDM capacity. Hypothesis: AI/HBM pressure is already visible in PTI utilization, pricing, capex, revenue mix, or customer allocation.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: 假设：随着 HBM 产能和先进封装资源被存储大厂优先分配给 AI 服务器需求，传统 DRAM/NAND 的封装、测试、burn-in、模组组装等后段产能可能受到挤出，进而把更多外溢订单推向第三方 OSAT。Powertech Technology 的潜在价值不在于它已经被证明是直接 HBM 核心供应商，而在于它可能处在被市场忽略的二阶瓶颈位置：当上游存储厂内部资源优先服务 HBM，高容量、成熟但仍必要的传统内存后段服务可能更依赖外包。当前公司官网和 TWSE 资料支持 PTI 是全球级 OSAT，服务覆盖 chip probing、packaging、testing、product delivery、memory 和 logic devices；公司官网财务资料显示 2025 年合并收入中 packaging 为 NT$50,200m，占 67%，testing 为 NT$16,662m，占 22%，SiP/Module 为 NT$8,067m，占 11%。但目前证据尚未证明这些收入增长来自 AI/HBM 外溢，也未证明 FOPLP、PiFO、CPO 或先进封装测试已构成实质收入。因此，本 thesis 在 Layer 5 仍应保持为“低到中等证据强度的产业链推理假设”，下一步必须用投资人会议、月营收、季报、客户披露、capex 和毛利率变化来验证。
deep_reports.thesis_en: Hypothesis: as memory IDMs allocate scarce internal back-end, engineering, and advanced-packaging resources toward HBM for AI servers, conventional DRAM/NAND assembly, test, burn-in, and module work may be crowded out and outsourced to third-party OSATs. PTI's potential edge is not that it is already proven to be a direct HBM chokepoint, but that it may sit in a second-order, underfollowed bottleneck: mature but necessary memory back-end work could be pushed outward when HBM absorbs internal capacity. Available evidence supports PTI's relevant supply-chain position: its own website and TWSE profile describe it as a leading provider of turnkey chip probing, packaging, testing, and product-delivery services for memory and logic devices. PTI's official financial page shows 2025 consolidated revenue by service of NT$50,200m packaging, or 67%; NT$16,662m testing, or 22%; and NT$8,067m SiP/Module, or 11%. However, the current evidence does not yet prove that these revenues are driven by AI/HBM overflow, nor that FOPLP, PiFO, CPO, or advanced-packaging/test revenue is material. Therefore, at Layer 5 this remains a low-to-medium evidence industrial-chain hypothesis that needs validation through investor-conference materials, monthly revenue, quarterly reports, customer commentary, capex, utilization, pricing, and margin signals.
deep_reports.title_cn: Powertech Technology：AI/HBM 后段产能外溢的二阶 OSAT 假设
deep_reports.title_en: Powertech Technology: Second-Order OSAT Hypothesis on AI/HBM Back-End Capacity Overflow
deep_reports.why_underfollowed: PTI may be missed by standard AI screens because it is usually categorized as a memory packaging/testing OSAT rather than as an AI accelerator, HBM stack, CPO, or advanced-packaging leader. The possible AI linkage is indirect and second-order: not 'PTI sells AI chips,' but 'AI-driven HBM resource prioritization may reshape outsourcing flows for conventional memory backend work.' This makes the signal less visible in headlines, keyword screens, and mega-cap-focused AI baskets. The market may also treat PTI's revenue recovery as a normal memory-cycle rebound unless company-level evidence shows capacity tightness, pricing power, or customer allocation changes tied to HBM/AI.

evidence_chain: Fact: Cohu describes itself as a global technology leader supplying test, automation, inspection and metrology products and services to the semiconductor industry. Source: https://ir.cohu.com/

Fact: Cohu states it is a leading supplier of semiconductor test handlers and contactors and a growing provider of automated test equipment, inspection & metrology solutions, and data analytics software. Source: https://ir.cohu.com/

Fact: Cohu’s website says its solutions support artificial intelligence, high-performance computing, automotive and autonomous systems, advanced medical equipment, and global connectivity. Source: https://cohu.com/

Fact: Cohu’s product portfolio includes equipment used to automate semiconductor device movement, control temperature during test, provide vision inspection, support ATE, provide contactors, and deliver AI-driven analytics for semiconductor manufacturers. Source: https://cohu.com/

Fact: Cohu’s investor-relations page listed an April 2, 2026 press release titled 'Cohu Announces $30 Million Follow-On Orders for High-Performance Computing Test.' Source: https://cohu.gcs-web.com/investor-relations

Fact: Cohu’s investor-relations page listed a May 12, 2026 press release titled 'Cohu Receives Multiple Orders for Testing Next-Generation GaN Power Devices for AI Data Centers.' Source: https://ir.cohu.com/

Fact: Public company-profile data describes Cohu as supplying test and inspection metrology automation systems, MEMS test modules, test contactors, thermal subsystems, data analytics software, ATE, handlers, interface products, probe heads and pins, and related services. Source: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/cohu/company/

Inference: Because AI/HPC and HBM devices increase package complexity, power density, signal-integrity requirements, and thermal constraints, back-end handling, contact, inspection, metrology, and thermal test may become more important chokepoint layers.
Hypothesis: Cohu’s AI/HBM-related products could become material enough to change investor perception if order flow, revenue mix, bookings, backlog, and margins show sustained AI/HPC contribution.

Unverified item: The provided evidence does not yet quantify Neon, Eclipse, HBM inspection, or AI/HPC handler revenue as a percentage of total company revenue; this must be checked in the latest 10-K, 10-Q, transcript, and investor presentation.
falsification_plan: Downgrade the thesis if the latest 10-K, 10-Q, earnings call, or investor deck does not contain meaningful references to HBM, AI, HPC, Neon, Eclipse, contactors, thermal test, inspection/metrology, or related product wins.
Falsify the upgrade case if HBM inspection and AI/HPC handler/contact/thermal-test products remain unquantified and immaterial for several quarters despite management commentary.
Downgrade if bookings fail to recover or backlog does not expand after announced HPC or AI data-center-related orders.
Downgrade if gross margin does not improve, or management attributes margin pressure to underutilization, pricing, or unfavorable mix despite AI/HPC product claims.
Falsify if legacy automotive, industrial, mobility, or broad semiconductor weakness continues to dominate revenue and margins, with no evidence of AI/HPC offset.
Downgrade if competitors announce more visible HBM inspection, handler, contactor, or thermal-test wins at major memory, foundry, logic, or OSAT customers.
Falsify if repeat orders do not follow initial AI/HPC or GaN AI data-center test announcements.
Downgrade if customer qualifications are delayed, cancelled, or limited to engineering samples rather than production-volume deployments.
deep_reports.hidden_signal_to_verify: The key hidden signal is whether HBM inspection and AI/HPC-related handler, contactor, thermal-test, ATE, or metrology products are moving from isolated design wins and small product-level orders into a recurring, material revenue stream. Specific upgrade evidence would include quantified HBM/AI/HPC revenue, repeat orders, backlog expansion, customer qualification for next-generation HBM or high-power AI/HPC packages, gross-margin uplift from mix, and management commentary that AI/HPC growth is offsetting weakness in automotive, industrial, mobility, or legacy semiconductor test.
next_research_tasks: Read Cohu’s 2025 Form 10-K and latest 2026 10-Q; extract every mention of AI, HBM, HPC, high-performance computing, GaN, data center, Neon, Eclipse, contactors, thermal, inspection, metrology, handlers, ATE, bookings, backlog, and gross margin.
Review the April 30, 2026 first-quarter earnings presentation and transcript; identify whether management quantified HPC, AI, GaN, or HBM-related revenue, orders, backlog, or customer count.

Open and parse the April 2, 2026 '$30 million follow-on orders for high-performance computing test' press release; determine product family, customer type, repeat-order language, shipment timing, and revenue recognition window.

Open and parse the May 12, 2026 'next-generation GaN power devices for AI data centers' order announcement; determine whether this is ATE, handler, thermal, contactor, inspection, or another product category.
Verify whether Neon and Eclipse are active Cohu product families tied to HBM inspection or AI/HPC handling; map each product to customer process step and revenue model.
Build a quarter-by-quarter table of revenue, bookings, backlog, gross margin, and end-market commentary from 2024 through the latest 2026 quarter.

Compare Cohu’s AI/HPC order language with competitors in handlers, contactors, inspection/metrology, ATE, probe cards, and thermal test to determine whether Cohu has differentiated exposure or is one of many suppliers.
Search customer-side or OSAT/memory/foundry capex commentary for HBM inspection, high-power AI package test, thermal test, and contactor bottlenecks.
Check whether announced orders are one-time tools, consumable-rich contactor/probe revenue, recurring service/software revenue, or platform placements that can create follow-on consumables.

Create an evidence upgrade ladder: Level 1 equals product mentions; Level 2 equals named order categories; Level 3 equals repeat orders/backlog; Level 4 equals quantified AI/HBM revenue; Level 5 equals margin and company-level revenue inflection.
risks: Materiality risk: AI/HBM-related products may remain too small to move total revenue, bookings, gross margin, or operating leverage.
Cycle risk: weakness in automotive, industrial, mobility, or legacy semiconductor test may overwhelm AI/HPC product growth.
Disclosure risk: management may discuss AI/HPC design wins without quantifying revenue, backlog, customer concentration, or margin impact.
Competitive risk: larger or more specialized test, handler, inspection, contactor, or metrology competitors may capture the main HBM and AI/HPC opportunities.
Qualification risk: AI/HPC and HBM production flows require customer qualification; delays, failed qualifications, or lack of repeat orders would weaken the thesis.
Margin risk: high-complexity products may not improve gross margin if pricing pressure, underutilization, integration costs, or service burden offsets mix benefits.
Narrative risk: the stock may already begin to price AI/HPC optionality before product-level evidence is strong enough, reducing the underfollowed edge.
Customer-concentration risk: a small number of AI/HPC or HBM customers could drive orders, creating volatility if programs pause or switch suppliers.
Technology-substitution risk: changes in package architecture, test flow, inspection method, or in-house customer capability could reduce Cohu’s attach rate.
Evidence-quality risk: current evidence supports exposure and order signals, but not yet a fully proven company-level AI/HBM revenue transition.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: AI supply chain node: downstream AI accelerators and HBM devices -> semiconductor manufacturing and OSAT/back-end process flow -> package/device inspection, metrology, handler automation, contactor interface, thermal control during test, ATE, process-control analytics -> Cohu as a supplier of semiconductor test automation, interface/contactors, inspection & metrology, ATE, thermal subsystems, and analytics. This is one to two steps away from the headline AI accelerator/HBM beneficiaries, making it a second-order chokepoint candidate rather than a direct AI compute supplier.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: 假设：AI/HPC 芯片与 HBM 器件的复杂度提升，会提高后段测试、检测、分选、接触器、热管理测试和计量环节的重要性。Cohu 被市场更多视为传统半导体测试设备、汽车和工业周期敞口公司，因此其 AI/HBM 相关产品线可能被低估。若 Neon、Eclipse、HBM inspection、AI/HPC handler、contactors、thermal test 或相关平台从小基数增长为可见收入，并能抵消传统市场疲弱，Cohu 的叙事可能从周期性测试设备供应商切换为 AI 半导体后段基础设施供应商。当前结论级别仍是 hypothesis，因为已知公开信号显示公司有 AI/HPC、test handling、contactors、inspection/metrology、thermal subsystems 和 data analytics 相关业务，但尚需验证产品级收入、订单、客户复购和毛利率贡献是否足够大。
deep_reports.thesis_en: Hypothesis: rising complexity in AI/HPC devices and HBM may increase the importance of back-end semiconductor test, inspection, handling, contactors, thermal test, and metrology. Cohu is often screened as a cyclical semiconductor test equipment supplier with automotive and industrial exposure, so the market may under-recognize its AI/HBM-linked product optionality. If Neon, Eclipse, HBM inspection, AI/HPC handlers, contactors, thermal test, or related platforms scale from small bases into visible revenue and offset legacy-market weakness, Cohu could be reframed as an AI back-end semiconductor infrastructure supplier. This remains a hypothesis, not a confirmed thesis: public evidence supports Cohu’s presence in test handlers, contactors, ATE, inspection/metrology, thermal subsystems, analytics, AI/HPC, and recent HPC/GaN AI data-center orders, but company-level materiality, product revenue, repeat orders, and margin contribution still need verification.
deep_reports.title_cn: Cohu：AI/HBM 后段测试、检测、分选与热管理的二阶瓶颈假设
deep_reports.title_en: Cohu: Second-Order AI/HBM Bottleneck in Back-End Test, Inspection, Handling, Contactors, and Thermal Test
deep_reports.why_underfollowed: Cohu is commonly categorized as a semiconductor equipment and test-handler supplier with cyclical exposure to automotive, industrial, mobility, and broader semiconductor capex. The AI signal is hidden at the product and customer-qualification level rather than in headline GPU, cloud, or accelerator revenue. The market may miss it because the relevant indicators are specific order announcements, product-family adoption, HBM/AI/HPC handler qualifications, contactor usage, thermal-test requirements, inspection/metrology attach rates, and mix-driven margin changes rather than simple AI revenue disclosure.

summary: Split Layer 5 deep reports generated one target at a time.
